criteria.text: Treatment of adults with paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH), the closed indication in this Alaska Medicaid criteria PDF.
Patient is an adult, 18 years or older (FDA labeled age; approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with a hematologist (approval criterion 2).
PNH diagnosis confirmed by flow cytometry diagnostic testing (approval criterion 3).
Documented baseline serum lipid panel (total cholesterol, LDL-C and triglycerides), hemoglobin, AND serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) (approval criterion 5).
Patient has tried and failed or has an intolerance or contraindication to one of eculizumab, pegcetacoplan, or ravulizumab-cwvz (approval criterion 6).
Vaccinated against Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, AND Haemophilus influenzae type B at least 14 days (two weeks) before the first dose (denial criterion 2).
Fabhalta will not be used in combination with another complement inhibitor (denial criterion 3).
No unresolved, serious infection caused by encapsulated bacteria, e.g. Streptococcus pneumoniae (denial criterion 4).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Fabhalta (iptacopan), a complement factor B inhibitor, Criteria Version 1: Original 03/13/2024; Accepted 04/19/2024; Effective 06/1/2024.

Encoded: closed adult PNH indication, approval criteria 1-6, and denial criteria 2-4 as approval-blocking predicates. Denial criterion 1 is failure to meet approval criteria. Hemoglobin <10 g/dL and baseline laboratory documentation are attestations.
Duration (notes only): initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization approval up to 12 months.
Quantity limit (notes only): 68 capsules in 34 days. Quantity and dosing are not evaluated as predicates.

Caution (notes only): increased susceptibility to serious, life-threatening, or fatal infections caused by encapsulated bacteria. Vaccination does not eliminate this risk despite antibody development.
Caution (notes only): after discontinuation, closely monitor for signs and symptoms of hemolysis for at least 2 weeks after the last dose.
Caution (notes only): use with cytochrome P450 2C8 (CYP2C8) inhibitors is not recommended.
Approval durations, reauthorization, quantity, dosing, and cautions require manual review; this pack remains partial.
No PDL hit; pdl_status remains unknown. Empaveli and Soliris/Ultomiris are linked complement inhibitor alternatives for PNH overlap only; their own criteria require separate review.
